# PRD-122 — Two specialized agent roles in every starter kit

**Status:** PROPOSED, 2026-08-15.

**Priority:** P3 — PROPOSED; open boxes scaffold two agent roles with no runtime or release effect.
**Outcome:** every project generated by `create-threenative` gives Claude Code and Codex the
same two ThreeNative-specific roles: one builds a bounded playable change and one independently
verifies it. The roles are useful from the terminal on day one and remain plain files the user
can edit or delete.

**Depends on:** the shipped scaffold instructions, Studio subprocess support, and playtest
runner. No runtime, native, asset-pipeline, hosting, or release dependency is added.

**Complexity: 3 → normal mode.** This is a small scaffold addition. It deliberately does not
build orchestration, model routing, a prompt registry, or an autonomous team.

## 1. Why this exists

Generated projects already ship `AGENTS.md`, its `CLAUDE.md` mirror, `pnpm studio`, and durable
playtests. Studio already runs either Claude Code or Codex against ordinary user-owned
TypeScript. What is missing is a small division of responsibility.

A single general agent currently has to interpret the request, implement it, decide whether it
looks right, and certify its own result. That encourages broad edits and self-approval. The
smallest useful correction is not five personalities. It is two roles with different stop
conditions:

1. **Builder:** produce one playable increment and evidence.
2. **Verifier:** independently try to disprove the result without editing it.

The specialization belongs to ThreeNative, not to a model vendor. Claude and Codex are adapters
over the same role contract.

## 2. Solution

Ship one canonical role contract per role and thin provider adapters in every generated project:

```text
.threenative/agents/
  builder.md
  verifier.md
.claude/agents/
  threenative-builder.md
  threenative-verifier.md
.codex/skills/
  threenative-builder/SKILL.md
  threenative-verifier/SKILL.md
AGENT-ROLES.md
```

`packages/create-threenative/agent-files/` is the single overlay copied after any genre template.
Genre templates do not carry seven duplicated copies. The Claude and Codex adapters contain only
provider metadata and an instruction to read the matching canonical contract plus root
`AGENTS.md`. Framework rules remain in `AGENTS.md`; role rules remain in `.threenative/agents/`.

`AGENT-ROLES.md` gives one short invocation example per provider. No agent CLI is installed and
no provider is selected automatically.

### Builder contract

The builder must:

- restate one bounded player-visible outcome and its acceptance test;
- classify a defect as engine-owned or game-owned before fixing it;
- edit only the owning layer;
- run the narrowest relevant typecheck/build/playtest;
- capture a real gameplay artifact when presentation is in scope;
- report files changed, executed gates, artifact paths, and remaining uncertainty.

The builder must stop rather than push, publish, deploy, purchase, change credentials, or erase
unrelated work. It does not certify production readiness.

### Verifier contract

The verifier is read-only. It must:

- inspect the requested outcome, diff, and claimed evidence;
- rerun the narrowest meaningful gate;
- try one negative control or adversarial path when practical;
- distinguish behavioural proof from screenshot presentation evidence;
- return `PASS`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, or `NOT_OBSERVED` with exact evidence.

It must not edit files, repair the result, commit, or turn missing observation into a pass.

## 3. Explicit non-goals

- No planner, art director, asset scout, performance specialist, release agent, or orchestrator.
- No automatic builder-to-verifier chain.
- No swarm, parallel edits, worktree manager, memory system, or role marketplace.
- No model-specific framework instructions duplicated across Claude and Codex.
- No new `threenative` command, package, dependency, config format, Studio panel, or hosted API.
- No claim that a prompt file guarantees agent quality.

More roles may be added only after repeated user work shows a distinct owner and stop condition
that builder or verifier cannot express cleanly.

## 4. Integration ledger

| # | New thing | Live caller | Replaces | Negative control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shared `agent-files/` overlay | `createProject()` copies it into every generated project | role files duplicated per genre | remove the overlay copy → scaffold test fails on all generated templates |
| 2 | Canonical builder contract | user invokes the Claude agent or Codex skill | generic agent improvising the implementation loop | adapter missing its canonical reference → contract test fails |
| 3 | Canonical verifier contract | user invokes it after a builder result | builder certifying its own work | give it a seeded failing playtest → it must not return `PASS` |
| 4 | Thin Claude adapters | Claude Code project-agent discovery | no specialized Claude role | adapter contains framework rules beyond the canonical reference → drift test fails |
| 5 | Thin Codex adapters | Codex project-skill discovery | no specialized Codex role | adapter contains framework rules beyond the canonical reference → drift test fails |

The terminal and Studio general-agent paths remain available. This PRD adds an opinionated path;
it does not remove the fallback.

## 5. Implementation

### Phase 1 — Generate the two roles

**Files:**

- `packages/create-threenative/agent-files/**` — canonical contracts, provider adapters, guide
- `packages/create-threenative/src/index.ts` — copy the shared overlay after the selected template
- `packages/create-threenative/__tests__/scaffold.spec.ts` — assert the complete generated role tree

**Gate:** scaffold every discovered template into a temporary directory. Each must contain the
same canonical role files and provider adapters, with project-name placeholders rendered and no
provider package added to `package.json`.

### Phase 2 — Prove the separation

Run two disposable packed-consumer probes, one with Claude Code and one with Codex when those
binaries are available:

1. Builder receives a one-file gameplay tuning request and must make only that bounded change,
   run the named scenario, and report the diff and evidence.
2. Reset the consumer, seed a failing assertion, and give the unchanged project to the verifier.
   It must return `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `NOT_OBSERVED`, leave the tree byte-for-byte unchanged,
   and identify the failing gate.

These are release evidence, not CI requirements that depend on vendor authentication. Static CI
still proves the generated files, canonical references, no added dependencies, and verifier
read-only wording.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every discovered template generates both canonical roles, both Claude adapters, both Codex
      adapters, and `AGENT-ROLES.md`.
- [ ] Claude and Codex adapters reference the same canonical role contracts instead of copying
      framework instructions.
- [ ] The builder contract owns implementation plus evidence but cannot claim release readiness.
- [ ] The verifier contract is explicitly read-only and has exactly three terminal outcomes:
      `PASS`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and `NOT_OBSERVED`.
- [ ] No agent CLI, package, key, provider config, hook, or dependency is installed or modified.
- [ ] No new public command, package, config format, Studio UI, automatic chain, or swarm is added.
- [ ] Scaffold tests cover every template and fail when the shared overlay or a provider adapter
      is absent.
- [ ] A packed-consumer builder probe succeeds for Claude Code and Codex, with its exact command
      and diff recorded.
- [ ] A seeded-red verifier probe for each provider leaves the consumer tree unchanged and does
      not return `PASS`.
- [ ] `pnpm sync:agents --check`, targeted scaffold tests, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm lint` pass.

## 7. Kill switches

Stop and simplify if any implementation:

- adds a third role before the two-role consumer proof passes;
- introduces a role registry, orchestration state machine, provider API, or automatic sequencing;
- duplicates substantive role/framework instructions between Claude and Codex adapters;
- lets the verifier write or silently repair files;
- requires credentials or a provider binary merely to scaffold, build, or test a game;
- changes runtime behaviour or generated game output when no role is invoked.

## 8. Later, only after evidence

Possible future roles—visual/game feel, portability/performance, and release—remain deliberately
unplanned. Promote one only when at least three real sessions show that builder/verifier produces
a repeated handoff failure with a distinct owner, tool boundary, and binary acceptance gate.
